title: fleet/list
description: Method `fleet/list`: the fleet catalog — the bundled registry snapshot crossed with passive local detection, plus user-declared custom agents. Populating the catalog never involves the network; detection is re-run on every query and never executes a binary.

fleetAgentSource.description: Where a catalog entry comes from: the bundled registry snapshot or the user's configuration.

id.description: Stable catalog identifier, selectable via agent.id in the project config.

integrationLevel.description: Declared Meltemi integration level (1 native ACP, 2 adapter, 3 structured headless, 4 artifacts).

verifiedLevel.description: The level verified by the last conformance run; absent means declared-but-unverified.

verifiedAt.description: The date of the conformance run behind verifiedLevel.

mcpSupport.description: Whether the agent declares MCP passthrough support in the registry.

detected.description: Whether the agent's binary was found on this system (PATH or candidate paths); detection never executes anything.

binaryPath.description: Absolute path of the detected binary; present only when detected.

configured.description: Whether the project at projectRoot selects this agent; always false when the request carried no projectRoot.

underlyingAgent.description: For a profile row, the catalog id of the underlying agent it launches; absent otherwise.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path of a project root; when given, the response marks the agent that project's configuration selects.

registryVersion.description: Version of the registry snapshot the catalog was built from (the substitute's version when the registry override is in effect).

agents.description: The catalog, in registry order with custom entries appended.

fleetLayerSource.description: Where a detected layer's binary was found: the user's PATH, a declared candidate path, or beside the running daemon (a layer that travels in Meltemi's own installers).

bundled.description: Whether the registry declares this layer as travelling in Meltemi's own installers; such a layer never carries a third-party install command.
